$comment: Request/response JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) for interceptor.postman_collection.json, rendered into its items' descriptions and INTERCEPTOR_SCHEMAS.md (linked from INTERCEPTOR.md). Edit here, then: uv run --no-sync python scripts/api_schemas.py render. A schema whose $comment says `generated from …` is rewritten by unit-tests/interceptor/test_api_schemas.py (API_SCHEMAS_UPDATE=1): never edit one. The rest is hand-written from app.py, profiles.py, logins.py and common.jobs (router.py, memory.py); that test validates the app's real responses against it, with a fake InterceptorClient in place of Chrome. The MCP envelope follows the MCP SDK's models (open objects) as FastMCP 3.4.5 fills them.

profile_name.description: Named Chrome profile: a directory under INTERCEPTOR_PROFILES_ROOT (profiles.py `_NAME_RE`)

profile.description: One profile's status; a profile with no directory is `present: false`, `size_bytes: 0` (a 200, not a 404)

present.description: The directory exists and is not empty

sentinel_present.description: The `session_ok` sentinel an upload writes: only a profile with it boots headless (absent when the directory does not exist)

login_keys.description: The credential reference names the profile's `login_actions` may use (`${username}`, `${password}`, …), from INTERCEPTOR_LOGINS_DIR/<name>.json; [] with no logins file. Never a value

login_origins.description: The logins file's `allowed_origins`: the origins a credential fill may type into; [] with no logins file

login_error.description: Why the profile's logins file is unusable (present only when it is)

profiles.description: Every directory under the root whose name is a valid profile name, sorted by name

interceptor_phase.description: `cloning` (slow path only, during the profile copy) → `capturing` → `cleaning_up`; `actions` while `page_script` / `actions` run (back to `capturing` when they finish)

interceptor_job.description: One in-flight capture: the shared `common.jobs` `JobBase` with the interceptor's own `metadata`. Completed captures are not retained

result.description: Never set: an in-memory job is gone from the registry once it completes

interceptor_jobs.description: The port pool and every capture currently running

cursor.description: An opaque token representing the current pagination position

capture_response.$comment: generated from app.CaptureResponse — do not edit

error.description: Why the step failed; 'skipped' when an earlier step failed (or the page never became ready) so it never ran.
error.title: Error

value.description: evaluate / page_script: the script's return value. DOM steps: details of the element acted on. screenshot: {format, mime_type, width, height, full_page, bytes, page_url, data_base64} (page_url is where the tab was at that step). scroll: {target, element?, scroll_top, scroll_height, client_height, at_bottom}.
value.title: Value

aborted_reason.description: null when every step ran (a failed screenshot step does not stop the run, so check each step's `ok`). Otherwise e.g. 'not ready: login page …', 'cancelled', 'actions[2] (click) failed: …', 'capture window ended before actions finished'.
aborted_reason.title: Aborted Reason

actions_report.description: What page_script / actions did — null unless requested. Screenshot images are on their steps' `value`.

login_actions_report.description: What login_actions did — null unless they were sent AND the capture hit a login wall. A fill reports only `value_length`.

ended_early.description: True only when the window ended before capture_window_seconds elapsed: stop_when_matched saw every pattern matched, or — with no url_patterns — the actions finished.
ended_early.title: Ended Early

job_base.$comment: generated from common.jobs.model.JobBase — do not edit
job_base.description:
Snapshot of one job at a point in time.

Fields:
    job_id: 12-char hex identifier assigned at registration.
    phase: Freeform string; each consumer defines its own convention.
        Interceptor-api uses ``"cloning" | "capturing" | "cleaning_up"``;
        classifier uses ``"staging" | "pending" | "processing" |
        "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled"``.
    created_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the job was registered.
    updated_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last phase / result / error
        transition. Equals ``created_at`` for a job that hasn't transitioned.
    elapsed_seconds: Wall-clock seconds since ``created_at``, computed at
        snapshot time from a monotonic clock. Present for ephemeral jobs;
        derived from ``created_at`` for persistent (SQLite-backed) jobs
        where the monotonic anchor is process-local and doesn't survive
        restarts.
    metadata: Consumer-defined dict describing the job. Typically the
        result of a pydantic ``BaseModel.model_dump()``.
    result: Populated on successful completion for persistent backends.
        Ephemeral backends never set this — a completed ephemeral job is
        already gone from the registry.
    error: Populated on failure for persistent backends. Same caveat as
        ``result`` for ephemeral.
job_base.title: JobBase

GET /v1/interceptor/health.description: Liveness only: no check of Chrome, the profiles volume or the port pool.

GET /v1/interceptor/profiles/:profileNam.description: A name that fails the profile-name pattern is a 400.

POST /v1/interceptor/profiles/:profileNa.description: Wipes the profile's directory first, then extracts the archive and writes the `session_ok` sentinel. A bad name, or an archive that does not unpack, is a 400; no `archive` field is FastAPI's 422.

archive.description: A .tgz / .tar.gz of a captured Chrome --user-data-dir (`tarfile.open(mode='r:*')`, so gzip / bzip2 / xz are detected); archive the CONTENTS of the profile dir (`tar czf x.tgz -C <profile_dir> .`)

schema.description: The profile as unpacked (no `login_keys` / `login_origins` here: GET /profiles/:profileName has them)

DELETE /v1/interceptor/profiles/:profile.description: Idempotent. A name that fails the profile-name pattern is a 400.

POST /v1/interceptor/capture.description: Every error is the generic `{"detail": "<message>"}`: 400 a bad profile name, `url_patterns` / `login_url_patterns` regex, action step or `login_actions` reference (or a missing logins file), 429 the port pool is exhausted, 500 no Chrome binary; a body the model refuses (an unknown step type, an 11th screenshot, an empty `url_patterns` with no screenshot step) is FastAPI's 422.

ClickAction.description:
Scroll the element into view and click its centre. `mouse` (default)
sends real pressed/released mouse events; `js` calls `el.click()`.

selector.description: CSS selector, matched in the document AND inside every open shadow root (Salesforce LWC / custom elements), each tree on its own — so `input` finds an input inside a component, but a descendant combinator never crosses a shadow boundary (`lightning-input input` matches nothing; use the host `lightning-input` — fill/select descend into it — or `input[name=...]`). The first VISIBLE match wins.

text.description: Optional filter on the matches: substring of the element's trimmed text (including text rendered in its shadow tree), value, aria-label, placeholder or title. Written `/…/flags` it is a JS regex.

ScreenshotAction.description:
Capture an image of the page as it is at this point in the run — after
a best-effort settle (~5 s) for a step that navigated. The image lands on
this step's `actions_report` entry as `value` ({format, mime_type, width,
height, full_page, bytes, page_url, data_base64}). A failed screenshot is
recorded (ok=false) and the run continues.

format.description: Image encoding. jpeg (default) is ~10x smaller than png for a typical page; png is lossless; webp is smallest but less universally decodable.
format.title: Format

quality.description: jpeg/webp compression quality. Ignored for png.
quality.title: Quality

full_page.description: Capture the whole scrollable document (clamped to max_height) instead of just the 1920x1080 viewport.

scale.description: Output scale factor. 0.5 halves both axes and roughly quarters the payload — use it when the image is going into an LLM context and pixel-level detail isn't needed.
scale.title: Scale

max_height.description: full_page only: cap on captured document height in CSS px. Chrome refuses clips beyond 16384.
max_height.title: Max Height

timeout_s.description: Budget for the whole step — settle, layout read and the capture itself (a tall full-page clip can take several seconds).
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

ScrollAction.description:
Set the scroll position on whichever container actually scrolls — the
document, or (Salesforce Lightning) an inner `overflow-y: auto` element,
shadow DOM included. Three forms, at least one of selector / to / by:
`selector` alone frames that element (`block`, default `start` = at the
top); `to` jumps to the top or bottom; `by` nudges by CSS px. With a
`selector`, `to` / `by` act on that element's scroll container. `click`
and `fill` centre their element, so a `scroll` right before a
`screenshot` frames it. Nothing to scroll is a no-op, not a failure.
`value`: {target ('window' | '<div class=…>' | null), element?,
scroll_top, scroll_height, client_height, at_bottom}.

The first VISIBLE match wins.

url_patterns.description: Regex patterns matched against every JSON XHR/fetch URL. Any capture whose URL matches at least one pattern is returned, bucketed by the first pattern that matched it. May be empty ONLY when `actions` has a `screenshot` step (a screenshot-only capture, whose window ends as soon as the actions finish).
url_patterns.title: Url Patterns

profile.description: Named Chrome profile under INTERCEPTOR_PROFILES_ROOT. Must be refreshed via POST /profiles/{name}/refresh first if the target requires auth.
profile.title: Profile

capture_window_seconds.description: How long to keep Chrome running to collect captures.
capture_window_seconds.title: Capture Window Seconds

keep_open.description: If true, leave Chrome running after the window. Useful for interactive debugging; the job also stays in GET /jobs until the operator manually kills Chrome (or POSTs /jobs/{id}/cancel).
keep_open.title: Keep Open

login_url_patterns.description: Regex patterns matched (re.search) against the tab URL AFTER navigation, to detect a redirect to a login wall. Omit to use the built-in defaults (login / signin / /auth). Because these are full regexes — not substrings — you can anchor one to a bare domain that a substring couldn't distinguish from an in-app URL, e.g. '^https?://roofix\.io/?$' matches the logged-out root but not 'roofix.io/project/...'. An empty list disables login detection.
login_url_patterns.title: Login Url Patterns

page_script.description: JS evaluated in the page once it is ready (before any `actions`). An EXPRESSION — use an async IIFE for multi-statement code; promises are awaited and the JSON-serialisable result comes back as `actions_report.page_script.value`.
page_script.title: Page Script

actions.description: Ordered browser steps (wait_for / fill / click / press / select / wait / evaluate / screenshot / scroll) run once the page is ready, so the page's own code fires the requests `url_patterns` is waiting for. Stops at the first failed step — except a failed `screenshot`, which is recorded and the run continues. At most 10 screenshot steps. `click` / `fill` centre their element, so a `scroll` right before a `screenshot` frames it. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Page scripts and actions and § Screenshots.
actions.title: Actions

actions_ready_timeout_seconds.description: How long the readiness gate (tab off about:blank, not on a login URL, document complete, capture hook installed) may wait before the steps are abandoned. Defaults to capture_window_seconds.
actions_ready_timeout_seconds.title: Actions Ready Timeout Seconds

stop_when_matched.description: End the capture window as soon as every `url_patterns` bucket has at least one match (and the actions, if any, have finished) instead of waiting it out. Requires url_patterns.
stop_when_matched.title: Stop When Matched

login_actions.description: Steps (wait_for / fill / click / press / select / wait / scroll — no evaluate or screenshot) run ONLY if the tab lands on a login wall (`login_url_patterns`), once per capture, to sign in; the session then continues to `url` as it would after a human login. A fill `value` may reference the profile's stored credentials as `${username}` / `${password}` (`$$` = a literal $) — they are resolved server-side from INTERCEPTOR_LOGINS_DIR/<profile>.json, and a fill only types into a page whose origin is in that file's `allowed_origins`. `${` anywhere else is a 400. `capture_window_seconds` must cover the login, the SSO redirect AND the target page load. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Login actions.
login_actions.title: Login Actions

login_actions_timeout_seconds.description: Upper bound on one login_actions run — the login page becoming ready plus every step (default 60). It runs inside capture_window_seconds, so the window must also be long enough for the login, the SSO redirect and the target page load.
login_actions_timeout_seconds.title: Login Actions Timeout Seconds

schema.title: CaptureRequest

200.description: `status` is the capture session's (`common.cdp_interceptor.ClientState`: `unlinked` / `loading` / `waiting_login` / `ok` / `error`) or `cancelled`; screenshots are base64 on their steps in `actions_report.actions[].value`

GET /v1/interceptor/jobs/:jobId.description: An id that is not in flight (never existed, or already finished) is a 404.

POST /v1/interceptor/jobs/:jobId/cancel.description: The POST /capture caller then gets a normal response with `status: "cancelled"`. 404 an id not in flight; 409 a capture already in `cleaning_up`.

was_phase.description: The phase the capture was in when the cancel landed

MCP initialize.description: The JSON-RPC response's `result` (streamable HTTP at `/mcp/`: one SSE `data:` message when the request accepts `text/event-stream`); the `mcp-session-id` response header names the session the later calls send back.

result.$comment: mcp.types.ListToolsResult: the SDK allows extra keys

items.$comment: mcp.types.Tool: the SDK allows extra keys

description.description: The tool's docstring: what the model reads

inputSchema.description: A JSON Schema: the arguments of `MCP <name>`

outputSchema.description: A JSON Schema of `structuredContent`: `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}` for the three `-> dict` tools; none for `capture_url`

MCP capture_url.description: The JSON-RPC response's `result.structuredContent` (one SSE `data:` message): POST /capture's body, except that a screenshot step's `value` has no `data_base64` -- `result.content` is that JSON as text, then a text label (`actions[i] screenshot — <page_url>, WxH`) and an image block per screenshot taken. Errors are data, never a JSON-RPC error: what POST /capture answers with a 400 / 422 / 429 / 500 comes back as this shape with `status: "error"`, `job_id: ""` and `error` saying why.

arguments.$comment: generated from app.mcp:capture_url — do not edit

profile.description:
Named profile under ``INTERCEPTOR_PROFILES_ROOT``. Discover
available names via the ``list_profiles`` tool. Profiles are
uploaded out-of-band by an operator (see INTERCEPTOR.md).

url_patterns.description:
List of regex patterns. Each intercepted XHR/fetch URL
is matched with ``re.search`` against every pattern; the response
body lands in the bucket of the first pattern it matches. May be
omitted only when ``actions`` has a ``screenshot`` step — then the
call ends as soon as the actions finish.

capture_window_seconds.description:
How long to run Chrome to collect captures
(default 20). Increase if the page fires XHRs late.

login_timeout.description:
Max seconds to wait for a login redirect to resolve
before returning ``login_wall: true``.

max_matches_per_pattern.description: Cap on how many bodies to return per pattern.

page_script.description:
JavaScript run in the page once it has loaded, before
any ``actions``. It is evaluated as an EXPRESSION; for several
statements use an async IIFE, ``(async () => { ...; return x;
})()``. Promises are awaited; the JSON-serialisable result comes
back as ``actions_report.page_script.value``. Use it to inspect
the DOM (e.g. list the form fields before writing ``actions``).
Do NOT use it to call the site's API with ``fetch()`` — sites that
sign their requests (CSRF tokens) refuse hand-made calls; drive
the form with ``actions`` instead.

actions.description:
Ordered steps run after the page is ready (off about:blank,
not on a login URL, fully loaded, capture hook installed). Each is
an object with a ``type``:
``{"type": "wait_for", "selector", "text"?, "state"?: "visible"|"attached", "timeout_s"?}``,
``{"type": "fill", "selector", "value", "text"?, "clear"?: true, "timeout_s"?}``,
``{"type": "click", "selector", "text"?, "method"?: "mouse"|"js", "timeout_s"?}``,
``{"type": "press", "key": "Enter"|"Tab"|"Escape"|…|<one char>, "selector"?, "text"?}``,
``{"type": "select", "selector", "value", "text"?}`` (native <select> only),
``{"type": "wait", "seconds"}``,
``{"type": "evaluate", "script", "timeout_s"?}``,
``{"type": "screenshot", "format"?: "jpeg"|"png"|"webp", "quality"?: 1-100, "full_page"?: false, "scale"?: 0-2, "max_height"?: 100-16384, "timeout_s"?: 30}``,
``{"type": "scroll", "selector"?, "text"?, "to"?: "top"|"bottom", "by"?: <px>, "block"?: "start"|"center"|"end"|"nearest"}`` (at least one of selector / to / by; to and by exclusive; block only with selector alone).
``selector`` is CSS matched in the document AND inside every open
shadow root (Salesforce Lightning / web components), each tree
separately — so a descendant combinator never crosses into a
component (``lightning-input input`` finds nothing; use
``lightning-input`` or ``input[name=x]``). First visible match
wins; ``text`` narrows it by visible text / value /
aria-label / placeholder / title (substring, or ``/regex/flags``).
``fill`` types into the real <input> inside a component host with
trusted keyboard input; ``click`` sends a real mouse click at the
element's centre. ``timeout_s`` defaults to 15. Steps stop at the
first failure — read ``actions_report`` to see which and why.
``screenshot`` captures the page as it is at that point (after a
short settle if the previous step navigated); put one after a
step to see what it did. Each comes back as an image block, in
step order, labelled ``actions[i] screenshot — <page_url>, WxH``,
and its metadata ({format, mime_type, width, height, full_page,
bytes, page_url}) is the step's ``value``. A failed screenshot is
recorded (``ok: false``) and the steps after it still run. At most
10 per call; prefer ``"scale": 0.5`` — it quarters the image and
is plenty to read a page. ``full_page`` captures the whole
document (up to ``max_height`` px) instead of the 1920x1080
viewport.
``scroll`` sets where the page is scrolled: ``selector`` alone
puts that element at the top of the frame (``block``); ``to`` /
``by`` (CSS px, negative is up) move the page's main scroller —
the document, or the inner container a Salesforce Lightning page
actually scrolls — or, with a ``selector``, that element's scroll
container. ``click`` and ``fill`` centre their element, so a
``scroll`` right before a ``screenshot`` frames it. Nothing to
scroll is a no-op (``target: null``), not a failure; the
``value`` reports ``scroll_top`` / ``scroll_height`` /
``at_bottom``.

stop_when_matched.description:
End as soon as every pattern has at least one
match and the actions have finished, instead of waiting out
``capture_window_seconds``. A click finishes when the mouse is
released, not when its request completes — if the page also makes
matching calls on its own, end ``actions`` with a step that waits
for the response you want — a ``wait_for`` on the element that
shows the result, or an ``evaluate`` that polls
``window._capturedResponses`` for a new entry (INTERCEPTOR.md §
Worked example) — plus a short ``wait`` so it reaches the service.

login_url_patterns.description:
Regexes ``re.search``-matched against the tab URL
after navigation to spot a redirect to a login page. Omit for the
defaults (``login``, ``signin``, ``/auth``); a list REPLACES them,
so include them yourself if you still want them. Add the site's
SSO host when it doesn't match those (Enphase:
``sso\.enphaseenergy\.com``) — otherwise an expired session
looks like an empty result instead of ``login_wall: true``. An
empty list disables login detection.

actions_ready_timeout_seconds.description:
How long the actions wait for the
page to be ready (loaded, off any login page) before giving up.
Defaults to ``capture_window_seconds``.

login_actions.description:
Steps that run ONLY if the page redirects to a login
wall (``login_url_patterns``), to sign in with the profile's
stored service account; the capture then continues to ``url``.
Same step objects as ``actions`` except ``evaluate`` and
``screenshot``. For the
credentials write REFERENCES — ``"value": "${username}"`` and
``"value": "${password}"`` — which the server fills in from its
own credentials file; ``list_profiles`` shows the reference names
(``login_keys``) each profile has. NEVER ask a user for a real
username or password and never put one in a step. Enphase:
``login_url_patterns=["login", "signin", "/auth",
"sso\.enphaseenergy\.com"]``, ``login_actions=[{"type": "fill",
"selector": "#username", "value": "${username}"},
{"type": "fill", "selector": "#password", "value":
"${password}"}, {"type": "click", "selector":
"input[type=submit].button"}]``. Raise
``capture_window_seconds`` (~120) so the login, the redirect and
the page load all fit; the result says what happened in
``login_actions_report``.
